description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three measures of accuracy—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for a set of LLMs. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," uses a linear scale ranging from 0.71 to 1.00, with tick labels appearing at intervals of 0.02. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," uses a linear scale from 0.0 to 1.0. The blue line with solid circles represents Final Accuracy, starting at approximately 0.85, peaking near 0.92 at an initial confidence of 0.82, then declining to about 0.87 by an initial confidence of 1.00. The green dashed line with circle markers represents Initial Accuracy, beginning at approximately 0.55, rising to a peak of about 0.85 at an initial confidence of 0.79, then generally declining to around 0.80 by an initial confidence of 1.00. The orange dashed line with diamond markers represents Δ Accuracy, which starts at approximately 0.38, drops sharply to about 0.05 at an initial confidence of 0.73, then fluctuates between approximately 0.05 and 0.40 before declining to around 0.05 by an initial confidence of 1.00. All lines are plotted with error bars indicating variability.
